issues: Dolphin is a flat solid cyan fill with dithering, lacking rim light and interior phosphor volume; reads as a CAD silhouette rather than a lit phosphor object

Glow halo around the dolphin is minimal, contributing to the flat, vector-like look

suggestions: Re-render the dolphin with a bright rim-light outline plus a softer, gradient/dithered interior so it reads as a glowing 3D phosphor form, not a flat fill
Scale the dolphin up and vertically center it so its arc spans ~50-60% of the 128px height, making it the unambiguous centerpiece
Remove or visually reconnect the floating fin/splash blob so the silhouette is continuous and clean
Add short, crisp persistence trails behind the dolphin's tail and body to convey OEL motion without fogging the scene
Dim the wave lines to 2-3 low-contrast rows occupying <15% height so they stay subordinate
Lower the contrast/brightness of the FFT bars and the right-side status text so the eye travels dolphin -> text -> waves -> FFT
Apply a subtle, tight bloom halo to the dolphin edges (crisp core, gentle glow) to match the real OEL phosphor look
